questions.question: A light microscope uses which type of illumination to magnify specimens?
questions.explanation: A light microscope is an optical device that uses visible light for illumination and lenses to magnify specimens.

questions.question: A microscope that utilizes a single lens for magnification is termed what?
questions.explanation: Simple microscopes utilize a single lens, while compound microscopes have a number of lenses in combination.

questions.question: Routine histological techniques involve which type of microscopy?
questions.explanation: All routine histological techniques involve the bright field microscopy.

questions.question: Which microscopy is best suited to observe unstained living cells?
questions.explanation: Dark field microscopy is where unstained specimens, such as living cells, are observed.

questions.question: Who invented the primitive microscope in 1673?
questions.explanation: Antonie Philips van Leeuwenhoek invented the concept of using convex lenses to magnify small structures in 1673.

questions.question: Who discovered and described the cell in 1655?
questions.explanation: The invention of microscope led to the discovery and description of cell by Robert Hooke in 1655.

questions.question: Which scientist invented the achromatic lens in 1829?
questions.explanation: Modern microscopy started with the invention of achromatic lens by Lister in 1829.

questions.question: Which optical part collects and focuses light onto the specimen?
questions.explanation: The condenser collects and focuses light from the light source onto the specimen being viewed.

questions.question: Which structure controls the amount of light coming through the condenser?
questions.explanation: The condenser has an aperture, or iris diaphragm, that controls the amount of the light coming up through the condenser.

questions.question: When the aperture is closed, how is the image affected?
questions.explanation: When the aperture is closed, light comes in the center and contrast is high.

questions.question: Where are the objective lenses attached on the microscope?
questions.explanation: Objective lenses are attached to the nosepiece of the microscope.

questions.question: Which component is responsible for magnifying the specimen initially?
questions.explanation: The objective lens is responsible for magnifying the specimen or section to be visualized.

questions.question: Which lens forms the real, inverted magnified image of the specimen?
questions.explanation: The real magnified image is formed by the objective lens.

questions.question: Which component produces the final virtual, erect magnified image?
questions.explanation: The eye piece produces a magnified virtual image which is seen by the eye.

questions.question: Which adjustment compensates for focusing differences between the user's eyes?
questions.explanation: Diopter adjustments are present to adjust the focusing of the eye piece.

questions.question: The body tube connects the eyepiece to the objective lenses and has what standard length?
questions.explanation: The body tube is a cylindrical tube that connects the eyepiece to the objective lenses with a standard length of 160 mm.

questions.question: Which part connects the body tube to the base of the microscope?
questions.explanation: The arm connects the body tube to the base of the microscope.

questions.question: Which knob brings the specimen into general focus?
questions.explanation: Coarse adjustment mechanical knobs bring the specimen into general focus.

questions.question: Which knob fine tunes the focus and increases the detail of the specimen?
questions.explanation: Fine adjustment fine tunes the focus and increases the detail of the specimen.

questions.question: Which structure holds the slide in place on the stage?
questions.explanation: Stage clips hold the slide in place on the stage.

questions.question: Which component supports the entire microscope?
questions.explanation: The base supports the microscope.

questions.question: The word compound in compound microscope refers to which feature?
questions.explanation: The word compound refers to the fact that two lenses work together to produce the final magnified image.

questions.question: Final magnification is calculated by multiplying the objective lens power by the power of which other lens?
questions.explanation: Magnification (M final) is calculated by multiplying M objective by M eyepiece.

questions.question: The unaided eye can distinguish two points separated by what minimum distance?
questions.explanation: A given sufficient light an unaided eye can distinguish 2 points lying 0.2 mm apart.

questions.question: Which factor increases the resolution of a microscope by using immersion oil?
questions.explanation: The resolution is dependent on the numerical aperture, where the refractive index of oil immersion is 1.51 compared to air which is 1.

questions.question: Which aberration produces a colored spectrum of white light?
questions.explanation: Chromatic aberration is the production of a coloured spectrum of white light.

questions.question: Which lens type fully corrects chromatic aberration for three colors?
questions.explanation: Apochromatic lenses are fully corrected for three colours.

questions.question: Which aberration is a defect of single lenses due to their curved surface?
questions.explanation: Spherical aberration is a defect of single lenses due to their curved surface.

questions.question: Which illumination method uses an auxiliary lens and iris to provide an evenly illuminated view?
questions.explanation: Kohler illumination provides an evenly illuminated view and displaces critical illumination.

questions.question: Which type of microscope illuminates the specimen from the side so it appears bright against a dark background?
questions.explanation: In dark field microscopy, scattered light enters the objective lens which results in bright objects against dark background.

questions.question: Which microscope utilizes a LASER scanned in an X-Y raster pattern?
questions.explanation: The confocal scanning optical microscope uses a LASER scanned across the object rapidly in an X-Y raster pattern.

questions.question: Which microscope uses ultraviolet light to excite fluorochromes in a specimen?
questions.explanation: In fluorescence microscopy, a fluorochrome is excited with ultraviolet light and the resulting visible fluorescence is viewed.

questions.question: An electron microscope uses what type of lenses instead of glass?
questions.explanation: Instead of glass lenses here one uses electromagnetic lenses.

questions.question: The resolving power of an electron microscope is approximately what value?
questions.explanation: The resolving power of an electron microscope is 0.2 nm.

questions.question: A transmission electron microscope passes a beam through sections thinner than what size?
questions.explanation: In transmission electron microscopy the beam of electron passes through the tissue which is a thin section less than 100 nm.

questions.question: A scanning electron microscope reflects electrons back from the surface to provide what type of view?
questions.explanation: In scanning electron microscope the beam of electrons is reflected back from the surface, thus giving us the surface view.

questions.question: Which step in tissue preparation maintains clear and consistent morphological features?
questions.explanation: The primary objective of fixation is that stained section of any tissue must maintain clear and consistent morphological features.

questions.question: Which commonly used fixative acts by creating a covalent bond between proteins?
questions.explanation: Formaldehyde is a cross-linking fixative which acts by creating a covalent bond between proteins in the tissue.

questions.question: Which process involves the removal of water from tissue using alcohol?
questions.explanation: Dehydration is the removal of water by a dehydrating agent, commonly alcohol.

questions.question: Which chemical is commonly used to clear tissue by removing the dehydrating agent?
questions.explanation: Clearing is making the tissue clear by removing the dehydrating agent, for example xylene.

questions.question: Paraffin wax is routinely used as an embedding medium and has what melting point range?
questions.explanation: Paraffin wax is routinely used as an embedding media and has a melting point of 45-55 degree.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to cut sections during routine histology?
questions.explanation: A rotary microtome is used to cut sections of 5-7 um thick for routine histology.

questions.question: What is the typical thickness of sections cut for routine histology?
questions.explanation: A rotary microtome is used to cut sections of 5-7 um thick for routine histology.

questions.question: Which basic dye is used to stain the nucleus blue?
questions.explanation: Haematoxylin is a basic dye and stains the nucleus blue.

questions.question: Which acidic dye is used to stain the cytoplasm pink?
questions.explanation: Eosin is an acidic dye and stains the cytoplasm pink.

questions.question: Which part of the microscope is the flat platform where the slide is placed?
questions.explanation: The stage is the flat platform where the slide is placed.

questions.question: What is placed over the stained tissue section to protect it on the slide?
questions.explanation: Stained tissue sections are mounted on a glass slide with a coverslip placed over it.

questions.question: The numerical aperture (NA) of a lens is calculated using which formula?
questions.explanation: The numerical aperture is calculated using the formula NA = n sin u.

questions.question: The refractive index of immersion oil used in microscopy is what value?
questions.explanation: The refractive index of oil immersion is 1.51.

questions.question: Which component controls the movement of the mechanical stage left, right, up, and down?
questions.explanation: Stage control knobs move the stage left and right or up and down.
